beliefs: f splits the input on whitespace runs, reverses each segment, and joins with single spaces [E1-E6]
Case and punctuation are preserved and reversed with their segment [E1, E2]
Leading/trailing whitespace is dropped and internal runs become single spaces [E3, E4]

The last output segment gets one extra copy of its own first character prepended (i.e. the original last segment's last character, duplicated at the start of the reversed last segment) [E5, E6, E7, E8]
The extra character appears only when the input has no leading or trailing whitespace; if the input is padded with spaces on either side, no duplication occurs [E9]
notes: E9 shows the duplication is suppressed when the raw input has leading or trailing whitespace (e.g. ' hi'->'iih' but 'hi '->'ih', '  hi  '->'ih'), so I gate the extra character on s == s.strip().
